prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” interior painting company for every homeowner — the right one depends on your home, budget, schedule and quality expectations. I can help you choose. Here’s a quick, practical approach and what to look for in St. Louis:

How to find the best company for you
- Search and compare: check Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi, Houzz and the BBB for local St. Louis painters. Look for companies with many recent 4–5 star reviews and responses to complaints.  
- Ask for referrals: friends, neighbors, or your local hardware/storefront paint supplier (Sherwin‑Williams, Benjamin Moore dealers) often know reputable contractors.  
- Get at least 3 written estimates that list prep, number of coats, paint brand/finish, and timeline.  
- Verify credentials: insurance (liability + workers’ comp), business license, and — for homes built before 1978 — EPA Lead‑Safe certification.  
- Check portfolio and references: ask to see recent interior projects similar to yours and call 2–3 past customers.  
- Compare warranties and cleanup policies: how do they handle touch‑ups and any missed spots?

Questions to ask every painter
- What paint brand, product line, sheen and number of coats do you use?  
- How will surfaces be prepped (filling, sanding, priming)?  
- Who will do the work — employees or subcontractors? Are they insured?  
- What’s the start date, projected finish date, and policy for delays?  
- Can you provide a written estimate and contract? Any warranty?

Red flags
- Only gives a rough verbal quote or asks for large upfront cash payment.  
- Extremely low price compared to other estimates.  
- No proof of insurance, no references, or poor/no online presence.

Typical cost & timeline (St. Louis, ballpark)
- Single bedroom or small room: roughly $300–$800.  
- Whole‑house interior (typical 3‑4 bedroom): $3,000–$10,000 depending on prep and quality of paint.  
- Most interior jobs take 1–7 days depending on size and prep needs.

Local options
- National franchises such as CertaPro Painters and WOW 1 Day Painting have St. Louis franchises and can be a good starting point for consistent processes.  
- Many excellent small, local contractors operate in St. Louis; the best way to find them is through local review sites and referrals.

If you’d like, I can:
- Look up and shortlist highly rated interior painters in a specific St. Louis ZIP code (you’ll need to allow me to search), or  
- Draft an email/phone script you can use when contacting painters, or  
- Help you compare any estimates you receive.

Tell me your ZIP code, the size/condition of the space, and your budget/finish expectations and I’ll help you next.
